newsitem.title: USA: Vitalink CEO resigns, company to take a charge.
newsitem.headline: Vitalink CEO resigns, company to take a charge.

text.p: Vitalink Pharmacy Services Inc said Monday that Gene Burleson has resigned as chief executive officer, effective immediately.

Vitalink expects to take about a $2.6 million non-recurring, after-tax charge in the first quarter of fiscal 1998 for severance and related expenses in connection with Burleson's resignation and the consolidation of all corporate functions in Naperville, the company said.

Donna DeNardo will continue to oversee the operations of the company in her position as president and chief operating officer until a successor to Burleson is named, the company, which provides medications, consulting, infusion and other ancillary services to customers with about 174,000 institutional beds as well as home infusion patients, said.
The company is considering both internal and external candidates, Vitalink said.

Vitalink also said its board of directors elected Essel Bailey Jr as director. Bailey is founder, chairman and chief executive officer of Omega Healthcare Investors Inc, a real estate investment trust.
